dedupe_keys.name: assessment of the impact of internet exchange points in kenya and nigeria 2012

description: This investment appraisal quantifies the benefits of two African internet exchange points, KIXP in Nairobi and IXPN in Lagos. Commissioned by the Internet Society and carried out by the consultancy Analysys Mason, the April 2012 study combined traffic, price and latency data with interviews of operators and content providers. For Kenya it found that KIXP localised more than 1 Gbit/s of peak traffic, cut latency for local traffic from 200 to 600 ms to 2 to 10 ms, saved local internet providers about 1.5 million US dollars a year on international links and helped mobile operators gain about 6 million dollars in data revenue. For Nigeria it found IXPN localised about 300 Mbit/s at peak, cut latency from 200 to 400 ms to 2 to 10 ms and saved operators more than 1 million dollars a year. Both exchanges drew a Google cache in 2011, and in Nigeria banks brought online platforms back from overseas hosting, while in Kenya the revenue authority's online services became faster. The report urged governments to support exchanges through sector reform. An updated study, Anchoring the African Internet Ecosystem, followed in 2020. Coverage: two national exchanges, around 2011. Format and access: report PDF on the Internet Society website, free. Licence: not stated for the report; the Internet Society website terms forbid reuse not expressly authorised without written consent; reuse terms therefore remain unverified. Simulation uses: cost-benefit appraisal of interconnection, network flow and latency modelling, and capacity planning of national exchanges. Related records: the PCH and Euro-IX directories and PeeringDB list exchanges and their members; the African Union AXIS project spread exchanges across Africa.
